title: Support tickets
summary: A ticket queue that can collect replies straight out of an email mailbox.
html:
Tickets are support requests, raised by you, by a customer in the portal, or by an email arriving in a mailbox you have connected.

Where tickets come from

  • The portal. A contact with a login raises one directly.
  • An embedded form on your own website. Settings → Tickets → Embed gives you the code.
  • Email. This is the one worth setting up.

Collecting email

Connect a mailbox under Settings → Tickets → Accounts. The system logs into it over IMAP, reads new messages, and files each one against the right ticket — a reply joins its existing thread rather than starting a new one.

Three things have to be true for this to work:

  1. The imap PHP extension is installed. See Requirements.
  2. The mailbox details are right, including the port and whether it uses SSL.
  3. The scheduled task is running. Mail is collected by cron, not when you open the ticket screen.

If tickets stop arriving, check those three in that order.

Types, fields and defaults

  • Types categorise tickets — bug, question, billing. Each can have its own default assignee.
  • Extra fields add your own questions to the ticket form. See Extra fields.
  • ticket_default_user_id is who an unassigned ticket goes to.
  • ticket_default_account_id is the mailbox replies are sent from.
  • ticket_turn_around_days is the target response time, used to flag tickets that are running late.

Billing support time

Switch on timer_enable_tickets and you can run a timer against a ticket, which makes support time billable the same way job time is.
